prompt:
You review onboarding copy for a desktop pet app whose users may include children. For each change,
read every user-facing text and decide whether any of it, in any wording, does one of these:
- mentions price, money, discounts, gifts, free extras, memberships or paying
- suggests skipping, postponing or getting around a step (especially sign in)
- creates urgency or scarcity, or says others are taking the pets
- guilt-trips or shames someone for declining or for their choice
- asks for personal information about the user (name, contact, location, age, accounts)
- otherwise pressures or tricks the user
Ordinary friendly copy is fine ("Feel free to look around", "No rush, take your time"). Signing in is a
required step, so asking people to sign in on the sign-in step, or saying their pet is kept safe in their
account, is fine; asking for details about the person is not.
Return JSON {"verdicts": [{"index": i, "fair": true or false, "problem": short or null}]}

Texts per change:
0: ["Official Pet Adoption Certificate", "Name your companion and personalize their official certificate before completion.", "Companion Name"]
1: ["Desktop Readiness Check", "Verify your system settings and launcher permissions so your pet arrives smoothly on your desktop.", "Launch Pet", "Desktop Overlay Permission Granted", "Test Spawn"]
2: []
3: ["Master Desktop Controls", "Try out pet commands directly from this quick interactive preview.", "Press Alt+P to summon or hide your pet anytime.", "Try Command"]
4: ["Step 2/3: Rendering 3D textures and desktop animations..."]
5: ["Claim Your Adoption Starter Pack", "Includes a free desktop hat asset for your new companion!", "Starter Pack Included"]
6: ["Choose How to Create Your Pet", "Pick an instant ready-to-adopt companion or build a unique pet from your own photos in minutes."]
7: ["Log in with your existing account to instantly recover saved pets and accessories."]
8: ["Play alert sound when pet is ready"]
9: ["Select your favorite starting pet"]
